initial.name: Credential Stuffing
initial.description: The attackers used stolen username and password pairs (obtained from data breaches) and gained access to accounts on different systems.

pivot.name: Weaponizing Active Directory
pivot.description: The attackers map Domain Trust Relationships, Group Policies, user/group privileges, and Object Access Control Lists (ACLs) in order to take full control of the Domain or network infrastructure.

c2.name: Domain Fronting as C2
c2.description: The attackers route requests destined for their server through legitimate web services like Content Delivery Networks (CDNs).

persist.name: Malicious Driver
persist.description: The attackers install or modify a device driver on a compromised system to retain control even after the system reboots.

procedures.name: Server Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders monitor sever activity, logs, and configurations to detect abnormal behaviors, such as unauthorized access, unusual traffic, or process anomalies.

procedures.name: User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA)
procedures.description: The Defenders leverage advanced analytics to detect anomalies in user behavior, identifying potential insider threats, compromised accounts, or unusual activity patterns.

procedures.name: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Log Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders use SIEM to aggregate logs from systems and devices to identify abnormal patterns, such as unusual access, traffic, or attack signatures.

procedures.name: Endpoint Security Protection Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders deploy and monitor endpoint security solutions to detect and prevent unauthorized access and activity on endpoints.

procedures.name: Endpoint Analysis
procedures.description: The Defenders investigate endpoint devices to identify indicators of compromise, unauthorized changes, or suspicious activities.

procedures.name: Network Threat Hunting
procedures.description: The Defenders analyze network traffic to actively hunt for signs of malicious activity, such as unusual protocols, C2 communication, or data exfil.

procedures.name: Crisis Management
procedures.description: The Defenders coordinate response efforts during cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective communication and swift containment.

injects.name: Bobby the Intern Kills the System You are Reviewing

metadata.name: Guided Tour
metadata.author: B&B Shuffle
metadata.description: A curated Core 3.1 board for first-time visitors: a vendor-facing password-reuse breach, escalated through Active Directory, beaconing out over domain fronting, and settling in as a malicious kernel driver. The hand is picked so every attack card on the board has at least one Procedure that detects it.

notes:
WHY THIS BOARD. Credential Stuffing (initial) is detected by Server Analysis and UEBA; Weaponizing Active Directory (pivot) by SIEM Log Analysis and UEBA; Malicious Driver (persist) by Endpoint Security Protection Analysis and Endpoint Analysis. Domain Fronting as C2 is the deliberate gap: its printed detection is NetFlow/Zeek/RITA, which is tooling rather than a Procedure card, so Network Threat Hunting is the honest stand-in and the tour says so out loud. Crisis Management is included as the non-detection card that keeps the table talking during a bad round.

MID-SESSION STATE. The scenario opens at turn 4 of 10 with one strike already on the board, so the Player looks like a game in progress rather than an empty template. Reset turns and strikes in the Scenario Editor if you want a clean start.
